title: Top Local Payment Methods in Indonesia: How Indonesians Pay
summary: From QRIS and e-wallets to virtual accounts and Alfamart, see how Indonesians pay online and in store, and how to accept every method with one integration.
body_markdown:
Indonesian shoppers pay in many different ways, moving between QRIS, e-wallets, virtual accounts, cards, cash at convenience stores, and PayLater depending on what they buy and where they buy it. For merchants, the lesson is simple: a card-only checkout misses most Indonesian shoppers.


This guide covers the seven payment method categories that matter most in Indonesia, who uses each one, and when to offer it, along with a recommended payment mix by business type. Each section links to our in-depth guide for that category.


Key takeaways:


- E-wallets lead online. In an April 2026 Snapcart survey, 44% of online shoppers said they use e-wallets for e-commerce purchases, ahead of cash on delivery (29%) and bank transfers or virtual accounts (20%).


- QRIS is the fastest-growing method. Its transaction volume rose 67.22% year over year in August 2026, and a single QR code accepts payments from any participating bank or e-wallet app.


- Cash is shrinking but not gone. Its share of in-store payment value fell from 77% in 2019 to 36% in 2025, and convenience-store payments let cash-preferring shoppers pay upfront instead of using COD.


- Cards are a small but high-value segment, best suited to travel, subscriptions, and foreign customers.


- There is no single best method. The right mix depends on what you sell, your average order value, and whether customers pay once or repeatedly.


## How Indonesians pay today


Indonesians now pay mostly with their phones. In an April 2026 Snapcart survey, 44% of online shoppers said they use digital wallets for e-commerce purchases, ahead of cash on delivery (29%), bank transfers or virtual accounts (20%), and cards (4%), according to


[Katadata Databoks](https://databoks.katadata.co.id/en/technology-telecommunications/statistics/6ab0decc53911/digital-wallets-emerge-as-indonesians-favorite-e-commerce-payment-method-in-2026) . Bank Indonesia data points the same way: QRIS transaction volume grew 147.65% year on year in Q3 2025.


In physical stores, the shift is just as fast.


[Cash fell from 77%](https://fintechnews.sg/128337/e-commerce/southeast-asia-payment-methods-2026-global-payments-report/) of point-of-sale value in 2019 to 36% in 2025, the fastest cash-to-digital move in Southeast Asia, driven by Bank Indonesia’s QRIS and BI-FAST rails.


The momentum has not slowed in 2026. Bank Indonesia recorded


[6.11 billion digital payment](https://ekonomi.bisnis.com/read/20260923/9/2006537/transaksi-qris-tumbuh-6722-pembayaran-digital-tembus-611-miliar-transaksi) transactions in August 2026, up 40.36% year on year, with QRIS volume growing 67.22%.


For merchants, the lesson is simple: a card-only checkout misses most Indonesian shoppers. This guide walks through the seven payment method categories that matter most, who uses each one, and when to offer it. Each section links to our in-depth guide for that category.


## **Indonesia’s top payment methods at a glance**


**Payment method** **Popular options** **Best for** **How the customer pays**

The options listed are those Xendit supports in Indonesia today; the market has more providers in each category.


## **1. QRIS: one QR code for every app**


QRIS (Quick Response Code Indonesian Standard) is Bank Indonesia’s national QR standard. One code accepts payment from any participating bank app or e-wallet, so a merchant no longer needs a separate QR for each provider.


It is also the fastest-growing payment method in the country. QRIS now reaches about


[69.3 million users](https://www.idnfinancials.com/id/news/69514/transaksi-qris-turis-asing-capai-rp6-2-triliun-hingga-agustus-2026) and nearly 46 million registered merchants, around 69% of them MSMEs . Transaction volume grew 67.22% year on year in August 2026.


QRIS also works across borders. Tourists from Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Japan, South Korea and China can pay Indonesian merchants with their home apps, generating 17.8 million inbound transactions worth IDR 6.2 trillion through August 2026 (same IDNFinancials source).


How it works: the customer scans a static or dynamic QR code with any QRIS-enabled app and confirms the amount. Online, you display the QR on the checkout page; in store, on a screen or a printed stand.


When to offer it: for in-store sales, small-ticket online payments, event and F&B businesses, and anywhere tourists shop. It is the easiest way to reach users of every wallet and mobile banking app with a single integration.


***Read also:***[QRIS Payments in Indonesia: A Complete Guide for Businesses](https://www.xendit.co/en-id/blog/qris-payments-in-indonesia-a-complete-guide-for-businesses/)


## **2. E-wallets: the default for mobile shoppers**


E-wallets are the most common way Indonesians pay online:


[44% of shoppers](https://databoks.katadata.co.id/en/technology-telecommunications/statistics/6ab0decc53911/digital-wallets-emerge-as-indonesians-favorite-e-commerce-payment-method-in-2026) in an April 2026 Snapcart survey said they use them for e-commerce purchases. The leading wallets are built into super apps for shopping, ride-hailing and food delivery. ShopeePay, embedded in Shopee, is the wallet


[68% of users](https://www.ipsos.com/en-id/mapping-digital-wallet-landscape-2026-which-platform-leads-users-preferred-choice-according-ipsos) turn to most for online transactions. Customers already hold a balance and use it often: about


[3 in 10 Indonesians](https://goodstats.id/article/5-platform-e-wallet-terpopuler-di-indonesia-2025-R1GNX) use an e-wallet daily, and 42% use one to save money.


The wallets that matter most:


- [GoPay](https://docs.xendit.co/docs/gopay) : part of the Gojek ecosystem, used daily for rides, food and online shopping.


- [OVO](https://docs.xendit.co/docs/ovo) : strong in retail, malls and e-commerce, with a large loyalty-points base.


- [DANA](https://docs.xendit.co/docs/dana) : a standalone wallet widely used for bills, top-ups and marketplace checkout.


- [ShopeePay](https://docs.xendit.co/docs/shopeepay-e-wallets-id) : tied to Shopee, the go-to wallet for shoppers who chase marketplace promos.


- [LinkAja](https://docs.xendit.co/docs/linkaja) and


[AstraPay](https://docs.xendit.co/docs/astrapay) : smaller user bases, backed by state-owned enterprises and the Astra group.


How it works: the customer picks a wallet at checkout, is redirected to the app, and confirms with a PIN. Payment confirmation is near-instant.


When to offer it: always, if you sell to consumers. E-wallets suit low-to-mid ticket, mobile-first purchases such as digital goods, F&B, travel add-ons and subscriptions. With Xendit, DANA, GoPay, OVO and ShopeePay can also be linked once and charged again for recurring or one-click payments. Wallet limits (up to IDR 20 million per transaction on most wallets) make them less suited for very large orders.


***Read also:***[E-Wallets: Indonesia’s Favorite Modern Payment Solution](https://www.xendit.co/en-id/blog/e-wallet-modern-payment-solution/)


## **3. Bank transfer via virtual account: trusted for bigger payments**


Bank transfers are the


[second-largest](https://www.worldpay.com/en/global-payments-report) online payment method, at 34% of e-commerce value in 2025 and forecast to reach 38% by 2030. Mobile banking is booming alongside: its transaction volume rose 47.08% year on year in August 2026, and BI-FAST, the national real-time transfer rail, processed 549 million transactions worth IDR 1,346 trillion that month.


For online checkout, the standard is the virtual account (VA): a unique account number generated for each customer or order. Because every payment lands against its own number, it is matched to the right order automatically, with no proof-of-transfer screenshots or manual checks.


How it works: the customer receives a VA number at checkout and pays it through mobile banking, internet banking or an ATM. Payment is confirmed as soon as the transfer arrives.


When to offer it: for higher-value purchases, B2B invoices, education fees, property and insurance payments, and customers who prefer to pay straight from their bank. Xendit supports VAs at 12 Indonesian banks, including BCA, Mandiri, BRI, BNI, Permata, BSI and CIMB, with limits up to IDR 50 billion per payment at most major banks.


***Read Also:***[Virtual Account Payments in Indonesia: A Business Guide to Smarter Bank Transfer Collection](https://www.xendit.co/en-id/blog/virtual-account-payments-in-indonesia-a-business-guide-to-smarter-bank-transfer-collection/)


## **4. Credit and debit cards: small share, high value**


Cards play a much smaller role in Indonesia than in most markets. Only about


[18.75 million](https://finansial.bisnis.com/read/20260721/90/1989601/prospek-bisnis-kartu-kredit-saat-transaksi-tumbuh-dua-digit) credit cards were in circulation in April 2026, barely changed from a year earlier. Getting a card requires income verification and a credit history, so cardholders tend to be higher-income consumers, and many shoppers skip cards entirely in favor of e-wallets, QRIS, virtual accounts or PayLater.


That small share is still valuable. Cardholders tend to spend more per order, and cards are the natural choice for travel bookings, international subscriptions, and customers from abroad. Domestic debit cards run on GPN (Gerbang Pembayaran Nasional), Indonesia’s national payment gateway, alongside Visa and Mastercard.


How it works: the customer enters card details at checkout and usually completes a 3D Secure check with their bank. Cards can also be saved for one-click and recurring billing.


When to offer it: for SaaS and subscriptions, travel and hospitality, premium retail, and any business selling to foreign customers. Card installments through partner banks can lift conversion on big-ticket items like electronics. Xendit accepts Visa, Mastercard, JCB, American Express, BCA cards and GPN in Indonesia, with installments and recurring payments supported.


***Read also:***[Credit Card Payments in Indonesia: A Complete Guide for Businesses](https://wordpress-595241-6541596.cloudwaysapps.com/en-id/blog/credit-card-payments-in-indonesia-a-complete-guide-for-businesses/)


## **5. Retail outlets: cash payments at Alfamart**


Cash has not disappeared from Indonesian e-commerce: 29% of online shoppers still pay by cash on delivery, according to an April 2026 Snapcart survey. COD carries real costs for sellers, with return rates


[2.5 to 3 times higher](https://www.mordorintelligence.com/industry-reports/indonesia-ecommerce-market) than prepaid orders. Over-the-counter (OTC) payment at convenience stores lets these shoppers pay in cash without the delivery risk of COD.


The two chains cover almost every neighborhood. Indomaret had more than


[24,000](https://databoks.katadata.co.id/perdagangan/statistik/6a13ad6a12188/toko-minimarket-di-ri-bertambah-pada-kuartal-i-2026-indomaret-terbanyak) stores by March 2026, and Alfamart operates over


[17,000](https://docs.xendit.co/docs/alfamart) .


How it works: the customer gets a payment code at checkout, visits any Alfamart or Indomaret store before the code expires, and pays the cashier. The merchant is notified as soon as the cashier confirms payment.


When to offer it: for customers without bank accounts or e-wallets, first-time online buyers, students, and sellers in gaming, education and digital top-ups. With Xendit, OTC payments range from IDR 10,000 to IDR 5 million per transaction.


***Read also:***[Retail Outlet Payments in Indonesia: A Strategic Guide for Enterprise Leaders](https://www.xendit.co/en-id/blog/retail-outlet-payments-in-indonesia-a-strategic-guide-for-enterprise-leaders/)


## **6. Direct debit: link once, pay again without friction**


Direct debit lets a customer link their bank account to your business once, then authorize future payments without re-entering account details or switching apps. It is a smaller category than wallets or VAs, but it solves a specific problem well: repeat and recurring payments from customers who prefer to pay from their bank rather than a card.


How it works: the customer links their account on first use and verifies with an OTP from their bank. After that, payments can be one-click or merchant-initiated on a schedule, depending on what the customer has agreed to.


When to offer it: for subscriptions, loan and insurance installments, utilities, and marketplaces with frequent repeat buyers. Xendit offers BRI Direct Debit in Indonesia, with support for recurring and merchant-initiated charges. For customers who prefer wallets, linked DANA, GoPay, OVO and ShopeePay accounts do the same job.


## **7. PayLater (BNPL): installments without a credit card**


PayLater, or buy now pay later (BNPL), is still a small slice of checkout: just 3% of online shoppers use it, according to an April 2026 Snapcart survey (


[Katadata Databoks](https://databoks.katadata.co.id/en/technology-telecommunications/statistics/6ab0decc53911/digital-wallets-emerge-as-indonesians-favorite-e-commerce-payment-method-in-2026) ). But it is growing fast. Bank-issued PayLater reached 32.80 million accounts and IDR 30.71 trillion outstanding by June 2026, up 33.54% year on year, according to OJK (


[Kontan](https://keuangan.kontan.co.id/news/pengguna-paylater-bank-capai-328-juta-outstanding-tembus-rp-3071-triliun) ), while PayLater financing from finance companies grew even faster, up 54.65% to IDR 13.62 trillion by July 2026 (


[Infobanknews](https://infobanknews.com/paylater-multifinance-makin-gemuk-ojk-wanti-wanti-hal-ini-ke-industri) ). OJK notes it is becoming a popular alternative to credit cards, especially among younger consumers.


How it works: the customer selects a PayLater provider, logs in or is approved in seconds, and chooses a tenor, often from 30 days up to several months. The provider pays the merchant and carries the credit risk; the customer repays the provider.


When to offer it: for electronics, fashion, travel, education and other purchases where a larger basket might otherwise be abandoned. It is especially useful for reaching the many shoppers who have a smartphone but no credit card. Xendit supports Kredivo, Akulaku, Atome and Indodana in Indonesia.


***Read also:***[PayLater (BNPL) Payments in Indonesia: A Complete Guide for Businesses](https://www.xendit.co/en-id/blog/paylater-bnpl-payments-in-indonesia-a-complete-guide-for-businesses/)


## **How to choose the right payment mix**


There is no single best method; the right mix depends on what you sell, your average order value, and whether customers pay once or repeatedly. As a baseline, e-wallets and bank transfers together cover about three-quarters of Indonesian online spend, and QRIS fills most of the gap in store.

A few practical rules help whichever mix you choose. Show the most popular methods first on mobile, since most shoppers pay from their phones. Use virtual accounts rather than manual bank transfer so payments reconcile automatically. Track success and drop-off rates per method, then add or reorder options based on what your own customers use.

## **Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)**


**What is the most popular payment method in Indonesia?**


Online, it is e-wallets, with 42% of e-commerce value in 2025, followed by bank transfers at 34%. In physical stores, cash is still the largest single method at 36% of point-of-sale value, but that share has halved since 2019 as QRIS and e-wallets take over.


**Which e-wallets should I accept first?**


GoPay, OVO, DANA and ShopeePay have the widest reach. LinkAja and AstraPay add loyal niche audiences at little extra effort once you are integrated with a payment gateway.


**What is the difference between a virtual account and a regular bank transfer?**


A regular transfer goes to your company account, so you must match each payment to an order by hand. A virtual account gives each customer or order its own number, so payments are identified and confirmed automatically.


**Is cash on delivery still necessary?**


COD still made up 13% of online payment value in 2025. Offering Alfamart payments lets cash-preferring customers pay upfront, which avoids the failed-delivery and cash-handling risks of COD.


**Which methods support recurring payments?**


Cards, linked e-wallets (DANA, GoPay, OVO and ShopeePay) and direct debit can all be charged again after the customer’s first authorization, which makes them the best fit for subscriptions and installments.
